subject: Short runway spike: request for interim burst allowance and prorated overrun handling
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightlane.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Maya Rao <maya@clearline.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week spike — short runway uplift ask

Hi Vivek,

Quick one — we kick off a special feature launch next Tuesday and expect a concentrated traffic spike for ~48-72 hours. Our estimate (attached) shows ~3.7x daily token volume for that window. We don’t have time to renegotiate a long-term commit; can Redwood do a short-term burst allowance or amortize the overrun across the next two invoices?

Ideal outcome: a temporary quota bump (or soft headroom) for the 72-hour window and either a grace rate or the ability to spread overrun costs across the next two billing cycles. Procurement is looped (Maya) for any PO/timing constraints.

Files: usage_report_May2025.csv attached (forecast + recent traffic).

Appreciate a quick read — our launch is time-boxed and we need confirmation by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Infrastructure
BrightLane AI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week spike — short runway uplift ask

Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the file.

We can support an interim uplift but need to lock a small set of terms to protect both sides. Quick clarifying Qs:
- Confirm window: 48 vs 72 hours? Your note says ~48–72; we need hard start/end timestamps.
- Is the traffic strictly bursty (short requests) or sustained higher concurrency?
- Priority: minimize app disruptions (latency) vs minimize invoice impact?

Looping in Karthik (pricing + SE) and Laura (finance) to propose a short-form option. If you can, send the exact launch start time and the billing contact for PO (Maya cc’d).

I’ll aim to get an offer that’s signable within a day.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: short-term burst pricing options for BrightLane

Vivek / Laura — reviewed Samir’s CSV. Highlights: forecasted peak 72h window, token increase 3.5–4x baseline, majority is inference (low context lengths). Two pragmatic offers we can present: 

Option A (Fast protective path)
- Temporary headroom: 2x committed quota for a 72-hour window starting at provided timestamp.
- Overrun capping: if additional consumption beyond 2x, cap overrun rate at 1.5x standard overage rate (no surprise surcharge).
- Billing: one-time true-up invoiced next cycle.
- Eligibility: no longer-term commitment required.

Option B (Incentivized amortization)
- Temporary headroom: 3x baseline for 72 hours.
- If overrun > baseline: offer 25% discount on overrun fees provided customer signs a 3-month commit extension (simple addendum).
- Amortization: spread the overrun invoice across next two cycles if payment terms allow.

Operational notes: we can enable prefix caching and slightly increase batching to reduce per-token cost during the window (SEs can implement quick prompts). Need a PO for any immediate large uplift.

Attachments: I’m prepping a short term-sheet (redwood_temp_burst_term_sheet.pdf) with exact language. Laura — any constraint if we put amortization on invoice vs discount?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Maya Rao <maya@clearline.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 72h interim headroom + amortized true-up (BrightLane)

Samir — following internal review, here’s a short, signable path so you can launch with confidence. We kept it minimal to avoid procurement overhead.

Term summary (72-hour window starting 2025-05-19T00:00:00-07:00):
- Temporary headroom: 2.5x baseline quota for 72 hours.
- Overrun handling: any usage beyond the 2.5x window will be invoiced at 1.4x the standard overage rate.
- Amortization: Redwood will split the one-time true-up across the next two invoices (if customer payment terms permit).
- Incentive: if BrightLane signs a 3-month commit addendum within 30 days, Redwood will credit 20% of the overrun back as a bill credit.
- Operational: SE-led batch/cache tuning to minimize cost; no changes needed from your side beyond launch coordination.

Attached: redwood_temp_burst_term_sheet.pdf (short-form language) and a DocuSign request link (docusign_signature_request.url).

Maya — for procurement, if you can confirm PO timing we’ll align the invoice schedule. If you prefer, I can send a PO-ready quote.

If that looks good I’ll fire the DocuSign for signature and we’ll unblock capacity on our side.

Best,
Vivek
From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightlane.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya@clearline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 72h interim headroom + amortized true-up (BrightLane)

Vivek — that structure looks reasonable and aligns with our needs. Two quick asks before signature:
1) Can the invoice split be 3-way (three invoices) instead of two? Our finance team prefers a longer smoothing window for cashflow.
2) Update invoice contact to billing@brightlane.ai (CC Maya).

If you can make those two tweaks in the short-form term sheet we’ll sign ASAP. I’ve forwarded the DocuSign to our procurement and they indicated this should be fast.

Thanks for turning on a customer-friendly option so quickly.

— Samir
